_comment: Maintainer-decision dispositions for issue #733 (launch-watch needs-human, 2026-11-16). The original scan records (reports/launch-watch/runs/2026-11-16-43840645824-1*.json) remain unchanged. Approved rows name the product identity for bring-up; the bring-up itself lands in its own PR through the standard scoped engine run. No score or rank is set here.

dispositions.name: Mastra → ai-coding
dispositions.reason: Mastra Forward is a forward-deployed services program: "A dedicated Mastra engineer, backed by a factory of agents in your repo". A staffed program is not an AI coding product, and Mastra's coding product, mastra-code, is already rostered in ai-coding (reports/launch-watch/2026-11-09-issue-671-review.json).
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-mastra-forward — headline quoted in issue #733; a dedicated engineer plus agents, a services offering.
open-rankings/ai-coding/products.json — mastra-code rostered.

dispositions.name: Mastra → device-agents
dispositions.reason: MCP Tasks lets agents continue during long-running MCP tool calls. A framework concurrency feature is not screen perception, input injection, or OS-level control of a real device; the keyword match (tasks, agent, agents) is lexical noise against the device-agents definition.
evidence: https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-mcp-tasks — headline quoted in issue #733: "Unblock your agents during long-running MCP tool calls."
open-rankings/categories.json device-agents definition: Agents that operate real phones and computers through hardware or OS-level control.

dispositions.name: Mistral → agent-skills
dispositions.reason: Rechecked live 2026-11-16: Vibe supports "preset or custom skills via open standards" and the docs point to creating a skill, but no browsable skill collection or plugin catalog is documented as a product surface, so the agent-skills definition (skill collections and plugin catalogs) is not met. Revisit if Mistral documents a catalog.
evidence: https://mistral.ai/news/vibe-agent/ — fetched 2026-11-16; "Reusable skills: extend Vibe with preset or custom skills via open standards."
https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/overview — fetched 2026-11-16; skill creation guides only, no catalog surface.
open-rankings/categories.json agent-skills definition: Skill collections and plugin catalogs that package reusable instructions and workflows for coding agents.

dispositions.name: Mistral → ai-code-review
dispositions.reason: Rechecked live 2026-11-16: the closest first-party wording is a docs bullet, "Review code: find bugs, logic errors, missing edge cases, and risky changes before they ship", an on-demand use inside the coding agent. No autonomous per-pull-request review product with summaries is documented, so the ai-code-review definition is not met. The ai-coding placement (this review, mistral-vibe) owns this launch.
evidence: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/overview — fetched 2026-11-16; "Review code" listed as an agent use case; Vibe "requests approval before sensitive actions".
open-rankings/categories.json ai-code-review definition: AI code review agents for every pull request: summaries, bug catching, and standards enforcement.

dispositions.name: Mistral Vibe → ai-coding
dispositions.reason: Approved as the distinct product identity mistral-vibe, not a generic Mistral identity. Verified live 2026-11-16: a shipped coding agent installable today (curl -LsSf https://mistral.ai/vibe/install.sh | bash, or uv tool install mistral-vibe, macOS/Linux/Windows), with a VS Code extension (publisher Mistral AI) and a web surface at chat.mistral.ai/code. The docs describe an agent that "can read files, run commands, write code, and open pull requests on your behalf, under your supervision", with API access through Mistral Studio. On-axis for ai-coding; the CLI, extension, and Studio API are the agentic surface. Bring-up runs the standard scoped engine run in its own PR.
evidence: https://mistral.ai/news/vibe-agent/ — fetched 2026-11-16; "Vibe is live at chat.mistral.ai."; "For code, Vibe is on the web at chat.mistral.ai/code, in VS Code through the new extension, and in your terminal with the CLI."
https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/quickstarts/vibe-code/install-cli — fetched 2026-11-16; install commands for macOS, Linux, and Windows; sign-in via Mistral account or API key.
https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/overview — fetched 2026-11-16; agent capabilities and per-agent configuration documented.
https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=mistralai.mistral-vibe-code — fetched 2026-11-16; "Mistral Vibe is an AI coding agent for VS Code that works across your whole project."

dispositions.name: Mistral → business-phone
dispositions.reason: The launch is a coding and productivity agent with a VS Code extension. It has no company numbers, call routing, SMS, or carrier compliance surface; the keyword match (extension, agent, productivity) is lexical noise against the business-phone definition.
evidence: https://mistral.ai/news/vibe-agent/ — headline quoted in issue #733; coding agent launch, no telephony.

dispositions.name: Mistral → data-pipelines
dispositions.reason: Search Toolkit builds "production search pipelines": retrieval infrastructure for search, not ELT that moves data from SaaS APIs, databases, and files into warehouses, so the data-pipelines definition is not met.
evidence: https://mistral.ai/news/search-toolkit/ — headline quoted in issue #733: "Production search pipelines, anywhere."
open-rankings/categories.json data-pipelines definition: Data pipeline and ELT platforms that move data from SaaS APIs, databases, and files into warehouses.

dispositions.name: Mistral → local-llm-runtimes
dispositions.reason: Timestral is a 209M-parameter probabilistic forecasting model that runs well on CPU. A model is not a tool for running large language models on your own hardware; the keyword match (model, cpu, models) is lexical noise against the local-llm-runtimes definition.
evidence: https://mistral.ai/news/timestral/ — headline quoted in issue #733: "State-of-the-art probabilistic forecasts with just 209M parameters, outperforming larger models on CPU."
open-rankings/categories.json local-llm-runtimes definition: Tools for running large language models on your own hardware across CPU, GPU, and Apple Silicon.

dispositions.name: Mollie → agentic-commerce
dispositions.reason: The launch adds American Express acceptance to Mollie in-person (POS) payments. Card acceptance at a terminal has no agent-facing catalog discovery, payment credential holding, or checkout, so the agentic-commerce definition is not met.
evidence: https://www.mollie.com/news/mollie-amex-pos-launch — headline quoted in issue #733; in-person payments acceptance.
open-rankings/categories.json agentic-commerce definition: Platforms and protocols that let AI agents discover catalogs, hold payment credentials, and check out.

dispositions.name: Mollie → business-phone
dispositions.reason: The launch integrates Mollie payments into HubSpot CRM. A CRM payments integration has no telephony surface; the keyword match (crm, hubspot, business) is lexical noise against the business-phone definition.
evidence: https://www.mollie.com/news/integration-hubspot-streamline-crm-payments — headline quoted in issue #733; payments initiated and tracked from HubSpot.

dispositions.name: Mollie → ecommerce-platforms
dispositions.reason: The launch expands Mollie's payment platform to the Baltics. Mollie processes payments for e-commerce businesses; it does not build or run online stores, so the ecommerce-platforms definition (storefront to checkout to fulfillment) is not met.
evidence: https://www.mollie.com/news/mollie-launches-baltics — headline quoted in issue #733; payment methods for e-commerce businesses, not a storefront platform.
open-rankings/categories.json ecommerce-platforms definition: E-commerce platforms for building and running online stores, from storefront to checkout to fulfillment.

dispositions.name: Mollie Connect → marketplace-payments
dispositions.reason: Approved as the distinct product identity mollie-connect, following the arena's stripe-connect and adyen-for-platforms pattern. The cited Bulgaria launch is a country expansion, but the marketplace-payments capability is documented first-party and verified live 2026-11-16: Mollie Connect covers merchant onboarding through Client Links with KYB, split payments that "distribute funds across multiple sellers in a single checkout, with upfront or delayed routing (Marketplaces)", monetization "via application fees or resell pricing (Platforms)", and OAuth-delegated authorization. docs.mollie.com publishes llms.txt, giving the agentic surface. Bring-up runs the standard scoped engine run in its own PR.
evidence: https://docs.mollie.com/docs/connect-overview — fetched 2026-11-16; Client Links onboarding with KYB, split payments and routing, application fees, OAuth; Connect for Platforms and Connect for Marketplaces documented.
https://www.mollie.com/products/connect — fetched 2026-11-16; payments, refunds, and payouts handled without leaving the platform.
https://docs.mollie.com/llms.txt — linked as the docs project index; public developer docs at docs.mollie.com.
open-rankings/categories.json marketplace-payments definition: Payfac-as-a-service for onboarding sellers, splitting funds, running payouts, and monetizing payments.

dispositions.name: Mollie → mcp-infrastructure
dispositions.reason: Rechecked live 2026-11-16: Mollie's MCP server is "a new tool that makes it easier for merchants and partners to integrate Mollie into their AI applications" by "making Mollie's APIs and tools accessible to AI clients". A first-party tool server for one vendor's own APIs is not the registry, gateway, or hosted tool-server layer the arena ranks. The announcement body also dates itself to July 2025, so it is not a current launch.
evidence: https://www.mollie.com/news/mollie-launches-ai-ready-mcp-server — fetched 2026-11-16; use cases are Mollie payment links, payment statuses, customer profiles, and mandates; body dated "Amsterdam, 29 July 2025".
open-rankings/categories.json mcp-infrastructure definition: The registry, gateway, and hosted tool-server layer of the Model Context Protocol ecosystem.
